dream: The card boiled past sixty, turning the air to wet paper. I pressed the dark oak down, but the wedge melted into a puddle under the heavy top edge. The slip drifted up through the melted stone, floating free of the roof I built. The Fat Tree leaned sideways, its branches too thick for the space, brushing against the lid. I stood on the flat anchor, which had shrunk to a thin line. Then I fell off the card entirely, landing on a dry floor I had never seen, where the cactus stood alone, biting at nothing.
